description: Australia's first fully integrated rare-earths refinery (Eneabba Phase 3): roasting, leaching, purification, solvent extraction and product finishing, producing separated Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb oxides - 'one of the few rare earths refineries operating outside of China' on commissioning. Capacity (AR25 p.57): 16.0 ktpa REO output on Eneabba stockpile feed (max 18 ktpa contained REO feed); 23 ktpa total REO capacity with all circuits on blended feed; FID (2022) modelled 17.5 ktpa. Owned and operated via Iluka wholly-owned SPE Iluka Eneabba Pty Ltd ('RefineryCo'). FID 3 Apr 2022 at A$1,000-1,200M and 2025 start; AR25: capital estimate now A$1.7-1.8B with >A$1B spent or committed (A$1,134M to date, A$443M in 2025), engineering >95% complete, civil works substantially complete, all major equipment ordered (roaster kiln due H1 2026), SMPEI contracts to be awarded H1 2026; commissioning 2027. Feedstock: Eneabba stockpile initially; Wimmera as potential future feed; third-party concentrates under contract from Northern Minerals (Browns Range) and Lindian (Kangankunde, 10% of capacity for 15 years). Offtake: binding customer agreements still being negotiated (A$400M EFA tranche conditional on offtake). Metallisation feasibility study to conclude in 2026; magnet-waste recycling at the refinery assessed as technically viable (2025 desktop study). CAPACITY SPLIT (added from the 5 May 2025 Investor Briefing, which the AR25 does not carry): Max TREO 23,000 tpa, NdPr oxide 5,500 tpa, Dy/Tb oxide 750 tpa. Under the Scenario C financing case (Eneabba stockpile + Balranald only) steady-state output is 15.1 ktpa TREO and 3.3 ktpa NdPr, so the 750 tpa Dy/Tb figure belongs to the fully-blended max case and not to owned feed alone.

description: RECLASSIFIED. This is NOT a commercial separation plant. USAR's FY2025 10-K states it twice: 'The Colorado Facility is not a commercial production facility, but rather develops and refines the technologies that, with success, would be applied at the Round Top Project', and in risk factors 'a development and demonstration facility, not a commercial production facility, and the technologies developed there may prove insufficient or prohibitively costly to scale.' Scale is given only as equipment count - '500+ planned mixer/settlers... one of the largest and most sophisticated solvent extraction demo facilities in the nation' - and the site is leased warehouse space with US$224k of total minimum lease payments to Mar 2028. Operations commenced 15 June 2026 to validate flowsheets for Round Top, third-party feedstock and magnet swarf recycling. On 14 July 2026 it produced commercial-grade dysprosium oxide and NdPr oxide SAMPLES from recycled Stillwater swarf - samples, at demonstration scale, with no tonnage and no revenue. The earlier claim held here of 'demonstrated production of commercial-grade Dy and NdPr oxide' was directionally right but overstated the node: it is a flowsheet validation, not capacity. CAPACITY NOT DISCLOSED and none should be inferred. The commercial nodes USAR describes are separate and unbuilt: 'the planned on-site Round Top processing facility and the Company's anticipated third-party MREC processing and magnet swarf recycling facility'.

description: The single most important node in the ex-China Dy/Tb chain: Lynas describes itself in the Q4 FY26 quarterly as 'the only commercial producer of light and heavy rare earth oxides outside of China'. Separates Kalgoorlie MREC into NdPr and, since the June 2025 quarter (Q4 FY25), Dy and Tb oxides - the first large-scale commercial Dy/Tb separation outside China. Quarterly Dy+Tb output remains small and volatile: 9 t (Q1 FY26), 26 t (Q2), 8 t (Q3), 19 t (Q4 FY26); the Q4 rise reflects both work-in-progress carried over from March and genuine recovery improvements. First samarium oxide produced March 2026 with customer qualification underway. The expanded HRE facility is staged product-by-product: gadolinium expected early FY28, yttrium early CY2028, then lutetium. RISK: the estimated cost of the expanded HRE facility rose from approximately A$180 million to approximately A$294 million including contingency, attributed to customer-specific purity and physical requirements, the higher cost of sourcing equipment outside China, and geopolitical cost escalation. No nameplate Dy/Tb capacity is disclosed. CAPACITY (added from the 29 Oct 2025 expansion announcement): the expanded HRE facility has processing capacity for up to 5,000 tpa of HRE FEEDSTOCK, with target nameplate annual processing capacity of Dy 250 t, Tb 50 t, Sm 1,100 t, Gd 400 t, Y 1,100 t and Lu 10 t (Y and Lu not recorded as capacities - no material node exists). Cost approximately A$180 million, self-funded from the September 2025 equity raising; the Q4 FY26 quarterly later revised this to approximately A$294 million. TREAT THESE NUMBERS WITH CARE: Lynas expressly states they are nameplate processing capacities on the planned equipment configuration, NOT production targets under ASX Chapter 5 and not forecasts, and that production at nameplate is subject to sourcing feedstock beyond Mt Weld - candidate sources named are Malaysian ionic clay deposits that do not yet exist as producing assets. Against FY26 actual output of 62 t Dy+Tb, the 300 t Dy+Tb nameplate is a roughly 5x step that depends on feedstock Lynas does not currently control. expected_start 2027 is INFERRED at LOW confidence from 'initial suite of separated HREs forecast to be available within 2 years' of Oct 2025, against a timeline expressly subject to regulatory approvals. FEED ENVELOPE: A HARD NULL, POSITIVELY VERIFIED. Lynas has NEVER published a class-level feed envelope for Kuantan. A sweep of the FY2023-FY2026 annual reports, FY25 and FY26 results presentations, the 2025 AGM presentation, Diggers & Dealers 2024/2025, all 2024-2026 quarterlies and the FY26 half-year found no mention of monazite, xenotime, mineral sands or bastnaesite as acceptable Kuantan feed, no mention of MREO, magnet swarf or any recycled feed, no tolling language, and no commercial terms for third-party feed. The strongest statements are class-less: 'Both Lynas Malaysia and the planned U.S. Rare Earths Processing Facility have been designed to accept third party feedstocks as they come online' (Jun 2024), and - now a STATED DEPENDENCY rather than an ambition - 'The HRE expansion project is required to process various kinds of HRE feedstock in addition to Mt Weld feedstock in order to produce target volumes of the suite of separated HRE products' (FY2026 Annual Report p.15). That independently confirms the arithmetic here: Mt Weld alone cannot fill the 300 tpa Dy+Tb nameplate. TWO PHYSICAL FRONT DOORS: the plant 'processes Mt Weld concentrate and mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC)' through cracking and leaching, solvent extraction and product finishing, with MREC receival facilities delivered as a Lynas 2025 capex item - so it can take either mineral concentrate or MREC. ONLY NAMED THIRD-PARTY COUNTERPARTY: a non-binding May 2025 MoU with Menteri Besar Inc of Kelantan for Malaysian ionic-clay MREC, which never reached definitive agreement and has since vanished from disclosure. REGULATORY FEED CONSTRAINT - THE MOST IMPORTANT NON-TECHNICAL FACT ABOUT THIS NODE: Malaysia's AELB has previously barred an entire feed class (lanthanide concentrate import and processing prohibited after 1 Jul 2023) and then re-permitted it ORIGIN-SPECIFICALLY (Oct 2023 variation, Mt Weld only, valid to 2 Mar 2026). The current licence, 3 Mar 2026 to 2 Mar 2036, carries NO feedstock-origin restriction - a loosening - but replaces it with a residue constraint: no WLP residue above 1 Bq/g after 2 March 2031, with an alternative cracking process to commence on an agreed plan by March 2028. Since WLP arises from acid cracking of thorium-bearing mineral concentrate, that is functionally a constraint on monazite-class concentrate feed unless the new process works, while MREC and ionic-clay carbonate enter downstream and carry little NORM - which is exactly where Lynas has been pointing. Treat that last step as inference.

description: CANCELLED. Lynas FY2026 Annual Report (26 Aug 2026), 'Lynas USA', p.16: funding for a new US supply agreement 'has been reallocated from funds previously intended for the construction of a HRE facility in Texas which will no longer proceed.' The pivot was announced five months earlier (ASX, 16 Mar 2026), which names the site explicitly: a binding Letter of Intent with the US Department of War to supply approximately US$96 million of light and heavy rare earth oxides over four years at a US$110/kg NdPr floor price, following 'the mutual decision to modify the original agreement... based on significant uncertainty as to whether the construction of the Heavy Rare Earth processing facility at Seadrift, Texas would proceed.' WORDING CAVEAT: Lynas never says 'cancelled', 'terminated' or 'abandoned' - the operative language is 'will no longer proceed', disclosed inside annual report narrative with no standalone announcement. NO IMPAIRMENT was attributable: FY26 impairment was A$1.7m on unrelated specific assets with no US attribution, and 'Seadrift' appears zero times in the FY26 annual report while 'Texas' appears once. Consistent with an expenditure-reimbursement contract under which little Lynas capital was at risk - FY26 government grants received were A$6.925m, netted against assets under construction. CORRECTION TO A FIGURE PREVIOUSLY HELD HERE: the DoD contribution was approximately US$258m ALLOCATED (FY2025 Annual Report p.15), not the ~US$288m 'received' reported in trade press. CAPACITY WAS NEVER DISCLOSED: no tpa figure for Seadrift appears in any Lynas document across FY2023-FY2026 annual reports, all FY26 quarterlies, the HY FY26 accounts or the 2022 and 2023 DoD award announcements. The secondary '2,500-3,000 tpa HREO' claim appears to be a conflation of two MALAYSIAN numbers - the 5,000 tpa HRE feedstock expansion at Lynas Malaysia and the 3,000 tpa JS Link magnet plant at Kuantan. Retained as a node for historical continuity and because the DoW funds were redirected rather than withdrawn; contributes zero capacity.

description: MP Materials' co-located separation complex at Mountain Pass, historically NdPr-focused. A heavy rare earth separation facility prioritising dysprosium and terbium is being added under a US$150 million DoD loan announced 10 July 2025, alongside a US$400 million DoD convertible preferred investment (DoD to become largest shareholder at approximately 15%), a 10-year US$110/kg NdPr price floor, and DoD offtake of 100% of the separate 10X magnet facility's output. CAPACITY: the Dy/Tb circuit has a stated nameplate of 200 MT/yr combined Dy+Tb, on approximately 3,000 MT/yr of feedstock throughput. FEED: MP has been producing and stockpiling its own SEG+ heavy rare earth concentrate at Mountain Pass since late 2023, and will also process third-party feedstocks; MP's SK-1300 technical report puts SEG+ at around 4% dysprosium and terbium, which on 3,000 MT/yr implies roughly 120 MT of contained Dy+Tb - BELOW the 200 MT nameplate, consistent with a plan to blend in richer third-party feed. TIMING HAS SLIPPED: commissioning was 'mid-2026' (Nov 2025), then 'expected in 2026' (FY2025 10-K), and is now 'in the second half of 2026' (Q2 2026 10-Q, 7 Aug 2026). PRODUCTION TO DATE IS ZERO: the Q2 2026 10-Q still speaks in the future tense, and MP publishes no Dy, Tb or HREE production KPI in any filing - only REO and NdPr volume (FY2025: 50,692 MT REO in concentrate, 2,599 MT NdPr oxide). MP separately signed a long-term offtake for separated gadolinium with an aerospace and defence customer (Q2 2026), with no volume or term disclosed. FEED ENVELOPE: the Q3 2025 'third-party feedstocks from emerging sources' line is the HIGH-WATER MARK for mineral feed and is never restated or elaborated in the FY2025 10-K or any 2026 filing - no material class is ever named for it. The ONLY third-party feed class MP does name for heavy separation is RECYCLED MAGNET MATERIAL: the FY2025 10-K describes midstream operations processing 'third-party feedstock, including recycled materials' and 'a commercial-scale, dedicated recycling line ... sourced from post-industrial and end-of-life magnets', and the Apple agreement covers 'scaled recycling capabilities at Mountain Pass' with, per the Q2 2026 10-Q, 'dedicated capacity for both NdPr and heavy rare earth separation'. NO named inbound feed supplier or feed agreement exists; the DoW commitment is assistance in procuring HREE feedstock, not supply. The Q2 2026 gadolinium offtake was OUTBOUND only. A market note by Adamas inside MP's own SK-1300 technical report explains the trade class MP is likely buying - 'Typical light rare earth separation facilities have too little Dy and Tb in their feedstock to economically justify ... heavy rare earth separation lines thus they precipitate these elements into a mixed SEG+ chemical concentrate for sale to plants with HREE separation capacity' - but that is third-party market analysis, not an MP statement about its own plant, and should not be tiered on. FEED ENVELOPE FOUND, BUT ONLY ON AN EARNINGS CALL. MP's COO named exactly two acceptable third-party classes in Q3 2025 Q&A: SEG+, and 'a full mixed rare earth carbonate with lights and heavies' - 'Our circuit can handle, because we have all of the capabilities, either one of those.' That is a genuine material-class envelope and it tiers MREC and SEG+ producers into this node. IT IS ALSO THE WEAKEST-SOURCED ENVELOPE IN THE GRAPH: MP publishes no transcripts, so the quote comes from a machine-generated third-party transcript and needs checking against MP's webcast replay. Nothing more specific has been said since - the Q2 2026 call reverted to 'feedstocks of different type and purity'. Positive nulls across MP's entire EDGAR corpus: monazite concentrate, ionic clay, MREO and MREC all return zero hits, and no named inbound feed counterparty or agreement exists anywhere. Watch a wording regression: 'the ability to process alternative feedstocks' appeared in the Q3 2025 10-Q and was DROPPED from the FY2025 10-K and both 2026 10-Qs.

description: The only fully licensed and operating conventional uranium mill in the US, and now the largest planned US Dy/Tb capacity. Current commercial capacity is up to 1,000 tpa separated NdPr oxide. Construction began July 2026 on a commercial-scale heavy rare earth expansion (capex approximately US$104 million, debt covered by a conditional US government loan commitment) adding up to approximately 120 tpa Dy and 20 tpa Tb oxide, plus 140 tpa Sm, 20 tpa Eu and 140 tpa Gd. The recorded capacities are the expansion's MAXIMUM DESIGN quantities, explicitly dependent on feed distribution and recoveries (release fn.2), and the Sm/Eu/Gd figures are not yet built. Dy and Tb circuits are targeted for completion by end 2027 with commissioning in Q4 2027; Sm/Eu/Gd circuits by end 2028, both 'depending on market needs'. A new MREC circuit will let the mill take heavy-rich third-party feedstocks and produce rare earth oxides and uranium simultaneously. A 2029 second expansion would raise capacity to 6,294 tpa NdPr, 80 tpa Tb and 288 tpa Dy, fed by all phases of Donald plus Vara Mada (Madagascar) and Bahia (Brazil). Downstream, output is intended to feed Energy Fuels' pending acquisitions - Australian Strategic Materials (metal/alloy, South Korea) and Vacuumschmelze (magnets, Sumter South Carolina, 2,000 t) - for an integrated 15,700 tpa REPM target.

description: HREE-focused refining complex built around Ucore's proprietary column-based RapidSX solvent extraction. A US$18.4 million DoD Phase 2 Award, formally kicked off 14 July 2025, funds construction of the first commercial-scale RapidSX machine at the site, running through commissioning, demonstration and 'Early Production' readiness of salable individual REE products. Under the preceding US$4 million Phase 1 Award, Ucore successfully separated terbium from dysprosium; US$3,352,884 of Phase 1 payments had been received with US$647,116 outstanding. Detailed design of the commercial columns is done at Ucore's Kingston, Ontario demonstration facility. No capacity or start date is recorded: the release states neither. CAPACITY (added from the 28 May 2026 engineering report): optimized configuration is an initial Machine A at approximately 600 tpa TREO plus three RapidSX Production Lines each up to approximately 3,000 tpa TREO, for approximately 9,600 tpa TREO overall; Machine A plus Line 1 gives approximately 3,600 tpa. All three recorded capacities are TREO THROUGHPUT on the same plant and SUPERSEDE one another - do not sum them. Ucore discloses no per-element Dy/Tb split, so this node still contributes zero to any attested Dy/Tb capacity total despite being an HREE-dedicated plant. PER-ELEMENT Dy/Tb CAPACITY: NOT DISCLOSED, and deliberately so. All 46 Ucore releases from Jan 2025 to Aug 2026 were enumerated; every capacity number is contained TREO in feedstock. The 28 May 2026 release lists the product suite as 'NdPr, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, SmEuGd (SEG), Tb, Dy, rare earth oxide products, and intermediates' with no tonnage against any element. The SMC is explicitly multi-feed and variable, which is why no split exists: the only Dy/Tb-bearing basket Ucore has quantified is the non-binding Aug 2024 Meteoric Caldeira MOU - 3,000 t TREO/yr containing over 900 t NdPr, approximately 6 t Tb and 24 t Dy (i.e. ~0.8% Dy, ~0.2% Tb of TREO), covering ~31% of nameplate and never restated against the current configuration. That is Caldeira's assemblage, not a design basis, and Aclara's much richer ionic-clay ratios must NOT be cross-applied. There is no NI 43-101 for the SMC (it is a processing facility, not a mineral project) and the Department of War techno-economic assessment that would contain a split is proprietary and withheld. STALE-DATA WARNING: the ucore.com/smc/ page still shows an obsolete '2,000 tpa 2026 / 5,000 tpa 2027 / 7,500 tpa 2028' staging superseded by the 28 May 2026 configuration - do not ingest it. QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE IS WEAKER THAN UCORE'S NEWS RELEASES SUGGEST. Ucore's Q1 2026 MD&A states that all seven DoD demonstration campaigns - SX-1 to SX-7, Dec 2023 to Jan 2026, 5,717 hours, 1.76 t REO equivalent - ran on a SINGLE heavy MREO feed source. No named third-party deposit is identified as having been processed in any campaign. The Wicheeda 'qualification' exists only in an April 2024 news release; Ucore's MD&A says merely that a sample was 'sent', in boilerplate unchanged for two years with no result, and Defense Metals' own filings never mention sending Ucore anything. On Ucore's own stated gate - process qualification 'over hundreds of runtime hours' - no third-party feed in this graph has been qualified. Treat every edge into this node as FEED_ENVELOPE at best. TWO NAMED PROJECTS HAVE PHYSICALLY SENT MATERIAL: ABx Deep Leads (a 10 g MREC sample, one of six recipients, Mar 2026) and Meteoric Caldeira (bulk pilot MREC for 'separation testwork and product qualification', Jun 2026). Neither counterparty discloses which Ucore facility received it, and neither reports any recovery, purity or separated product - only 'highly favourable feedback'. Meteoric moreover names MTM Critical Metals, not Ucore, as its separation testwork partner. Hastings/Wyloo sent nothing: their Yangibana HoA expressly contemplates building a hydromet plant to convert concentrate to MREC first, and UCORE HAS DISAPPEARED FROM HASTINGS DISCLOSURE after 13 Mar 2026, over which period Hastings pivoted to a 49%-owned Thai hydromet plant on African monazite - no filing says whether the HoA lapsed, was extended, or stands.

description: Proposed separation plant on leased land at the Grupa Azoty Pulawy chemical complex, designated one of 47 EU CRMA Strategic Projects on 25 Mar 2025. PFS (19 Mar 2026, PRODEO Consulting, base date 25 Feb 2026, AACE Class 4 +/-25%): expanded base case of 30,000 t/a MREC feed at 45% TREO wet basis with 100% NdPr separation, 13,430 t/a REO throughput, capex US$212.4M including US$35.4M contingency, opex US$2.142/kg TREO in MREC, NPV US$779.1M at 10% nominal, IRR 39.7% nominal, payback 2.12 years. KEY FINDING FOR Dy/Tb: this is most likely NOT a Dy/Tb node. The PFS product suite is Nd oxide, Pr oxide, NdPr oxide, SEGH carbonate and LaCe carbonate - dysprosium and terbium are not separated products but report to a mixed SEGH (Sm-Eu-Gd-heavies) carbonate, and the study's only optionality is the NdPr split (0/50/100%), with no HREE circuit variants. The 50 t/yr Dy/Tb oxide figure survives only in the year-earlier CRMA release for the smaller original design and is recorded at LOW confidence as an unreconciled conflict between two primary Mkango documents. FEED ENVELOPE CONFIRMED, and the arithmetic hypothesis was right: Pulawy is DESIGNED around third-party feed. Mkango's SEC F-4/A states it plans 'to source MREC from other rare earth projects and market suppliers', and that the plant 'is expected to rely on third-party carbonate feed in addition to the MREC sourced from Songwe Hill'. BUT NO IMPURITY SPECIFICATION IS PUBLISHED and Mkango itself flags off-Songwe chemistry as unresolved metallurgical risk, and there is NO third-party feed agreement - 'or at all'. So the route in is stated but unpriced and unproven.

description: Aclara's 100%-owned US separation plant, named Project Dynamo, at the Port of Vinton, Louisiana - the step that turns Carina from a concentrate producer into an integrated Dy/Tb supplier. Scoping study released 13 Apr 2026 as a COMPANION to the Carina FS on the same day (which is why it appeared absent when only the FS release was read). Annual average output at >99.5% purity: 148 t Dy oxide, 25 t Tb oxide, 1,131 t NdPr oxide, on Carina-only feed; heavier elements (Y, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu) and Sm/Eu/Gd leave as mixed carbonates in Phase 1. Phasing: Phase 1 NdPr/Dy/Tb; Phase 2 Y, Gd, Sm; Phase 3 the remaining heavies, market-dependent. Economics: construction capex US$277M plus US$52M working capital, after-tax NPV US$470M at 8%, IRR 25.2%, payback 3.3 years, opex US$12.6/kg TREO processed against a US$40/kg processing fee. Louisiana incentives US$46.4M as estimated in Oct 2025, of which the ITEP component received FINAL state approval on 26 Jun 2026 at approximately US$20.8M over the initial 5-year term - below the US$29.3M originally estimated. Schedule: FEL-3 basic engineering Q3 2026, long-lead awards Q4 2026, construction Q1 2027 to Q1 2028, pre-commissioning and ramp-up from Q2 2028; key permits (air, industrial wastewater, stormwater) targeted October 2026 with groundbreaking Q4 2026. STUDY-STATUS CAVEAT: this is scoping level, a full study grade below the Carina FS, and its NPV is excluded from that FS. UNRECONCILED: the Carina FS books a US$314.4M average annual separation fee (34% of Carina gross revenue) payable to this facility, while Dynamo reports average annual NET revenue of US$175M on a US$40/kg processing fee - the two do not reconcile on their face and likely use different bases (gross transfer price vs net revenue booked). Resolve from the filed NI 43-101 before either enters the graph as a revenue fact. Also note a double-count trap in Aclara's separate 50/50 metals and alloys JV with CAP: its '154 t FeDy metal' is an 80%Dy:20%Fe alloy, not 154 t of dysprosium. CAPTIVE BY DESIGN - a negative finding worth as much as an envelope. Every FILED Aclara document says Dynamo processes Aclara's own material: the AIF states 'Aclara Technologies intends to source high-purity mixed MREC from the Company's mining projects', and 'The pilot plant has been specifically designed based on the characteristics of the Carina Project MREC production.' The only third-party statement anywhere is a single unfiled marketing bullet - 'Third-party compatible MREC processing' - with no tonnage, spec, timeline or capacity, explicitly excluded from the economics. The structural tell is that Dynamo pays THIRD PARTIES to separate its own by-products, which is not merchant behaviour. Moving the feed intermediate from MREC to SPREC at approximately 99% RE content further tunes the front end to Carina chemistry - Aclara's stated purpose is to strip impurities upstream because they are 'the main source of complexity in the solvent extraction plant'. Aclara nowhere says this narrows the envelope; that inference is ours. DO NOT create third-party CAN_SUPPLY edges into this node.

name: SARECO / Summit Atom Rare Earth Company (Stepnogorsk)
location_description: Stepnogorsk, Kazakhstan; includes approximately 15,500 sq m of warehousing, land and associated assets
description: A node this graph was missing entirely, and a structurally important one: an ALREADY-CONSTRUCTED AND OPERATIONAL MREC plant outside China, previously owned and operated by Sumitomo Corporation and Kazatomprom, which Lindian took to 100% ownership on 10 Aug 2026 for US$20 million cash (reported total consideration up to US$42 million with equity and performance rights). Lindian's claim, verbatim: 'SARECO is the only constructed and operational MREC/CLP Processing Facility of commercial scale outside of China, MP Materials Inc., Serra Verde and Lynas Rare Earths Ltd.' IT SITS ONE LEVEL UPSTREAM of the Dy/Tb separators in this graph: it converts monazite concentrate into MREC at ~92% TREO / ~97% NdPr recovery (96% overall NdPr recovery from Kangankunde concentrate), it does NOT separate individual oxides, and it therefore contributes ZERO Dy/Tb capacity while potentially feeding several plants that do. facility_type BENEFICIATION is imperfect - the function is hydrometallurgical cracking and leaching, matching how Lynas Kalgoorlie is typed here, but neither is truly beneficiation. NAMEPLATE CAPACITY NOT DISCLOSED in the acquisition release; the only throughput figure is the ~12,500 tpa of Kangankunde concentrate expected to feed it. Target MREC production Q4 2026. GEOPOLITICAL CAVEAT: Kazakhstan is recorded as NEUTRAL alignment at LOW confidence - it is landlocked between Russia and China, so physical routing of both feed and product is itself a supply-chain exposure that a chemistry-only reading of this node will miss. IDENTITY AND HISTORY CORRECTED: the full legal name is Summit Atom Rare Earth Company LLP; the original JV was KAZATOMPROM 51% / SUMITOMO CORPORATION 49% (not Toshiba, as circulating secondary accounts have it), opened 2 November 2012 at Stepnogorsk in the Akmola region, originally recovering rare earths from URANIUM-ORE RESIDUE. Flowsheet is sulphuric acid bake, water leach, impurity removal, carbonate precipitation. THE LARGEST UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION IN THIS NODE: Sumitomo's 2012 release gives an original nameplate of 1,500 t/yr of rare earth product, while feeding 12,500 tpa of 55% TREO concentrate implies roughly 6,875 t of contained TREO per year - about 4.6x that nameplate. Lindian has never disclosed a current capacity in either the 3 Mar 2026 or 10 Aug 2026 announcements, and no primary document reconciles the gap; either the plant is being substantially expanded or the 12,500 tpa is aspirational. FEED IS NOT SOLELY KANGANKUNDE: on 31 Aug 2026 Lindian optioned a 13,389 t Aktau heavy-rare-earth stockpile with 12-month exclusivity over a further 15,000-20,000 t, explicitly processable 'ahead of, alongside or independently from Kangankunde concentrate deliveries' - which both loosens the Kangankunde over-commitment and makes SARECO a potential Dy/Tb source in its own right, since the Aktau material is described as HREE-bearing.
